passes.poem:
The chamber holds a single note of stone,
Where dust performs a silent, patient dance.
A chair, upholstered in forgotten bone,
Waits for a guest who never takes a chance.

The mirror shows a room without a name,
And every shadow sharpens like a blade.
A clock unwinds the hours into shame,
While spiders weave a pact no light has made.

The floorboards creak a language of the lost,
The ceiling bows beneath a weight of sighs.
And in the center, where the cold is crossed,
A broken breath still waits to realize.

Trembling.
Hushed, waiting.
Echoes, dust, stone.
Echoing, patient, dance, chair.
In bone, a guest waits.
Lost, the mirror sharpens like blade.
Each shadow weaves a pact no light.
Even hours unwind the floorboards creak language.
No name, a clock unwinds into shame, spiders.
Languid, the ceiling bows beneath a weight of sighs.
And in the center, where the cold is crossed, broken.
Underneath, a breath still waits to realize what never came.

Trembling  
Hushed waiting  
Echoes dust stone  
Echoing patient dance chair  
In bone a guest waits  
Lost the mirror sharpens like blade  
Each shadow weaves a pact no light  
Even hours unwind the floorboards creak language  
No name a clock unwinds into shame spiders  
Languid the ceiling bows beneath a weight of sighs  
And in the center where the cold is crossed broken  
Underneath a breath still waits to realize what never came.

passes.poem:
The chamber holds a single, patient breath,
Where dust motes dance in one forgotten shaft.
The walls are ears that listen past all death,
And keep the echo of a single draft.

A chair sits empty, turned to face the door,
Its velvet faded to a mourning gray.
A clock has stopped at half-past-four, before
The final guest was led or lost the way.

The silence here is not a thing of peace,
But pressure waiting for a latch to turn.
The shadows learn the room by heart, and cease
To question what the candlelight might burn.

The
chamber holds
every patient, single breath,
Where dust motes dance in one forgotten shaft.
In walls are ears that listen past all death,
Lest they keep the echo of a single draft.

A chair sits empty, turned to face the door,
Its velvet faded to a mourning gray, still.
A clock has stopped at half-past-four, before
The final guest was led or lost the way, and

Now silence here is not a thing of peace,
But pressure waiting for a latch to turn, so
Loud the shadows learn the room by heart, and cease
To question what the candlelight might burn, yet

All the shadows learn the room by heart, and cease
Until they question what the candlelight might burn.
